rules.paraphrase: Invoices are submitted monthly within 30 days of period end and final bills within 30 days of the settlement agreement.
Actual time is billed in increments no greater than 1/10 hour; minimum charges above 0.1 hour are not acceptable.
Narrative and block billing is not permitted; each task is separately identified with its own time.
Entries describe persons involved and work performed in enough detail to show purpose and necessity; calls state participants and subject.
Each entry shows timekeeper, date, hours, description and amount; invoices are chronological, one matter each, with a summary by timekeeper and rate.
Electronic invoices carry a unique number, the UC matter number, UTBMS expense codes and dates; reused invoice numbers are rejected.
At most two core attorneys and one paralegal bill most time; occasional billers stay under 10 percent; only approved panel attorneys bill.
Rates are approved within set ranges, unilateral increases are not accepted and contract staff mark-up may not exceed 20 percent.
Consistent billing of more than 7 hours a day or 150 hours a month by one biller on a case must be justified.
Two billers should not perform the same task; only one attorney bills for meetings and only the senior person for office conferences.
Learning, training, clerical, administrative, conflict, scheduling and audit-response work is overhead and not billable.
Routine research is not billable and research beyond three hours per case needs prior approval.
Photocopies at actual cost not above ten cents a page, showing the number of copies, the page rate and the total.
Travel at UC policy rates, coach air fare, meals only on authorised overnight travel, travel time net of commuting.
Phone, fax, routine postage, subscriptions, database costs, entertainment and unsupported disbursements are not reimbursed.
Vendor invoices up to 5,000 dollars are paid by the firm and then billed at cost.

unmapped_provisions.paraphrase: Required use of the extranet knowledge base before billing for new research.
An initial budget is due within 60 days (litigated) or 45 days (non-litigated); invoices above budget need an updated budget.
